body_md: Export Rust with `#[wasm_bindgen]` and import JS with `extern "C"` blocks. Numbers cross directly; strings are encoded in linear memory. Keep the boundary narrow for speed.
hook: Exports out, imports in — one macro each way.

quiz.explain: wasm_bindgen attribute exports; extern C block declares JS imports.
options: Exports use macro, imports use extern block
quiz.q: How do you declare exports vs imports?

takeaway: Export with the macro, import with an extern block.
trap: Marking large structs Copy across the boundary; clone costs add up.

body_md: js-sys mirrors JavaScript builtins like Array, Map, Date, and Promise as Rust types. Use it instead of raw `js_value` juggling when you need collections or reflection from Rust.

quiz.explain: js-sys provides typed bindings for standard JS objects.
options: It binds JS builtins like Array and Map

takeaway: Reach for js-sys when touching plain JS values.
trap: Holding JsValue across await without Send checks in workers.

body_md: web-sys binds Web APIs: DOM, canvas, fetch, audio. Enable only features you use like `Document` or `HtmlCanvasElement` to keep compile times and binaries small.

quiz.explain: Each Web API is gated behind a Cargo feature.
options: APIs are feature-gated to control size
quiz.q: How does web-sys keep binaries lean?

takeaway: Enable only the web-sys features you actually call.
trap: Enabling all web-sys features explodes build times.

body_md: Grab elements by id, create nodes, and set text without JS. web-sys methods return Option and Result, so unwrap carefully and cache handles instead of querying each frame.

quiz.explain: web-sys exposes create_element and query APIs with Result types.
options: Use web-sys document APIs from Rust
quiz.q: Can Rust WASM manipulate the DOM directly?

takeaway: Manipulate DOM from Rust via web-sys handles.
trap: Querying DOM every frame instead of caching nodes.

body_md: Call `fetch` from Rust with web-sys plus wasm-bindgen-futures. Await the promise, convert to `Response`, then parse JSON with serde. Always map JS promise rejections to Rust errors.
hook: fetch in Rust, parse with serde.

quiz.explain: JsFuture turns a JS Promise into a Rust future.
quiz.q: How do you await fetch from Rust WASM?

takeaway: Bridge promises with JsFuture then deserialize.
trap: Forgetting CORS still applies to WASM fetch calls.

body_md: Derive Serialize and Deserialize for structs crossing fetch. Use `serde-wasm-bindgen` to convert JsValue without JSON strings when speed matters. Validate shapes before unwrapping.
hook: Structs across the boundary without manual parsing.

quiz.explain: Serde maps structs to JSON or JsValue deterministically.
quiz.q: How should Rust structs cross the JS boundary?

takeaway: Let serde generate conversions for API types.
trap: Changing field names without serde rename breaks JS.

body_md: Draw with canvas via web-sys: get context `2d`, set fill style, and call fill_rect. For animation, hook `requestAnimationFrame` with a Closure and mutate state each tick.
hook: Pixels from Rust, no JS needed.

quiz.explain: Canvas contexts are exposed as typed web-sys objects.
options: Get canvas context via web-sys and draw
quiz.q: How do you draw to canvas from Rust?

takeaway: Fetch the context once, then issue draw calls.
trap: Resizing canvas without resetting transform blurs output.

body_md: Pass Rust closures to JS with `Closure::wrap`. It boxes a FnMut and gives a JS function pointer. Use it for event listeners and animation frames with explicit lifetime control.
hook: Rust closures as JS callbacks — handle with care.

quiz.explain: Closure::wrap creates a JS-callable handle for a Rust closure.
options: Closure::wrap boxes Rust closures for JS
quiz.q: How do you pass a Rust closure to JS?

takeaway: Wrap callbacks so JS can invoke Rust code.
trap: Dropping Closure too early silences events mysteriously.

body_md: Leaked closures are the top WASM memory bug. If JS must call back later, call `closure.forget()` to intentionally leak, or store it in a struct. Otherwise drop it after registration for one-shots.
hook: forget() is a feature, not a bug — sometimes.

quiz.explain: forget leaks intentionally so JS keeps a valid function pointer.
options: Leak with forget when JS retains the callback

takeaway: Leak only callbacks JS must keep calling.
trap: Forgetting every closure causes slow memory growth.

body_md: Strings cross as pointer plus length in linear memory. wasm-bindgen mallocs, writes UTF-8, and JS decodes. Avoid round-tripping huge strings in hot loops; pass indices instead.
hook: Strings are pointers wearing a costume.

quiz.explain: Strings are UTF-8 bytes shared via allocated memory ranges.
quiz.q: How do strings cross the WASM boundary?

takeaway: Treat string passing as allocation plus copy.
trap: Holding a &str view after memory.grow invalidates it.

body_md: Typed arrays share memory without copying. Use `js_sys::Uint8Array::view` for zero-copy reads or `new_with_length` plus `copy_from` for safe copies. Views dangle if memory grows, so scope them tightly.

quiz.explain: Uint8Array views map directly onto linear memory.
quiz.q: What is the efficient way to move bytes to JS?

takeaway: Prefer typed-array views for bulk bytes.
trap: Keeping a view alive across memory growth corrupts data.

body_md: Async Rust works with `wasm-bindgen-futures::spawn_local` and `JsFuture`. Do not block the single UI thread; split work into tasks and yield. Use channels to report progress back to the DOM.
hook: Async without threads on the main loop.

quiz.explain: spawn_local schedules futures on the browser event loop.
quiz.q: How do you run async Rust in the browser?

takeaway: Bridge JS promises and drive them on the event loop.
trap: Blocking the event loop freezes rendering entirely.

body_md: Handle JS exceptions as `JsValue` or `Result<_, JsValue>`. Use `#[wasm_bindgen(catch)]` on fallible imports so throws become Err instead of traps. Log with `console_error_panic_hook` in dev.
hook: JS throws become Rust Results with one attr.

quiz.explain: catch converts JS exceptions into Err values.
quiz.q: How do you handle JS exceptions in Rust?

takeaway: Mark fallible imports catch to avoid hard traps.
trap: Panicking across the boundary aborts without useful stacks.

body_md: Keep the boundary chunky, not chatty. Each call crosses serialization and JS engine costs. Batch updates into structs or buffers, cache object handles, and move tight loops fully into Rust.
hook: One fat call beats a thousand thin ones.

quiz.explain: Fewer, larger calls amortize boundary overhead.
options: Batch work into few chunky calls
quiz.q: How do you minimize interop overhead?

takeaway: Batch data and compute on one side before crossing.
trap: Calling per-pixel setters from Rust kills frame rate.

body_md: Debug with browser devtools source maps plus `console_error_panic_hook::set_once()`. It forwards Rust panics to console with stacks. Pair with `wasm-pack build --dev` for readable names.
hook: Readable panics instead of cryptic traps.

quiz.explain: The hook formats panic info into console.error.
quiz.q: How do you get useful Rust panic messages in the browser?

takeaway: Install the panic hook early in development builds.
trap: Shipping the hook to production leaks internals.
